lessons.title: Solving quadratic equations
lessons.programRef: Cameroon secondary (general education) Mathematics programme, Form 4 (MINESEC) — to be checked against the official programme
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use the discriminant to decide the number of roots
Form and solve quadratic equations from problems
reviewNotes: Simultaneous equations with a quadratic and quadratic inequalities are not covered.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Factorising
blocks.md: Write the equation as $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ (zero on one side), factorise, and use the fact that **if a product is zero, one of the factors is zero**. $x^2 - 5x - 14 = 0$ gives $(x - 7)(x + 2) = 0$, so x = 7 or x = −2. Always give **both** roots and check them.

blocks.title: The quadratic formula
blocks.md: When factorising is hard, use the formula for $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$:

blocks.caption: The graph of y = 2x² − 3x − 4 meets the x-axis at about 2.35 and −0.85.
blocks.alt: A U-shaped curve crossing the x-axis at −0.85 and 2.35.

blocks.title: The discriminant
blocks.md: The number $b^2 - 4ac$ is the **discriminant**. If it is positive there are **two different** real roots; if it is **zero** there is one repeated root; if it is **negative** there are **no real roots** (the curve does not touch the x-axis). For $2x^2 - 3x - 4 = 0$: 9 + 32 = 41, so x = (3 ± √41) ÷ 4 = 2.35 or −0.85 (2 d.p.).

blocks.title: Completing the square
blocks.md: To solve $x^2 + 6x + 2 = 0$: move the constant: $x^2 + 6x = -2$. Add (half of 6)² = 9 to both sides: $(x + 3)^2 = 7$. Take square roots: $x + 3 = \pm\sqrt{7}$, so $x = -3 \pm 2.646$, that is x = −0.35 or −5.65 (2 d.p.).

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Solving x² = 5x by dividing by x: this loses the root x = 0; write x(x − 5) = 0.
- Forgetting that −b and the whole numerator are divided by 2a.
- Using the formula with the equation not equal to zero.

blocks.title: Example 2: a fenced plot
blocks.statement: A rectangular plot at Bamenda has perimeter 36 m and area 80 m². Find its dimensions.
steps: Half the perimeter: length + width = 18, so length = 18 − w.
Factorise: (w − 8)(w − 10) = 0, so w = 8 or w = 10. The plot is 8 m by 10 m.

lessons.title: Direct, inverse, joint and partial variation
lessons.programRef: Cameroon secondary (general education) Mathematics programme, Form 4 (MINESEC) — to be checked against the official programme
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Write and solve direct variation y = kx and y = kx²
Write and solve inverse variation y = k/x
reviewNotes: The gas tariff is invented for practice; it is not a real price list.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Direct variation
blocks.md: y **varies directly as** x (y ∝ x) when y = kx: doubling x doubles y. k is the **constant of variation**. If y = 12 when x = 3 then k = 4, so y = 4x and when x = 7, y = 28. The graph is a straight line through the origin. Variants: y ∝ x² means y = kx²; y ∝ √x means y = k√x.

blocks.title: Inverse variation
blocks.md: y **varies inversely as** x (y ∝ 1/x) when y = k/x, or xy = k. If x doubles, y halves. If y = 6 when x = 4 then k = 24, so y = 24/x and when x = 3, y = 8. The graph is a curve called a **hyperbola** that never touches the axes.

blocks.caption: Graphs of y = 4x (direct) and y = 24/x (inverse) for x from 1 to 6.
blocks.alt: A rising straight line and a falling curve crossing at about x = 2.45.

blocks.title: Joint and partial variation
blocks.md: **Joint**: y varies as x and inversely as z gives y = kx/z. **Partial**: y is the sum of a fixed part and a varying part: y = a + bx. Use two data pairs to find a and b. Method for every problem: 1. write the equation with k; 2. find k from the given pair; 3. rewrite with k; 4. substitute to answer.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Writing y = x + k instead of y = kx for direct variation.
- Confusing inverse variation with a negative gradient: xy stays constant.
- Using only one pair of values to solve a partial variation: two pairs are needed.

blocks.title: Example 1: direct and inverse
blocks.statement: (a) y ∝ x and y = 12 when x = 3. Find y when x = 7. (b) y ∝ 1/x and y = 6 when x = 4. Find y when x = 3.

blocks.title: Example 2: workers and partial variation
blocks.statement: 8 workers finish a job in 12 days. Days vary inversely with the workers: how long for 6 workers? A cooking gas supplier charges C = a + bn FCFA for n units; the bill is 7 000 for 10 units and 11 500 for 25 units. Find a and b.
steps: Days × workers = 8 × 12 = 96, so 6 workers need 96 ÷ 6 = 16 days.
blocks.answer: **16 days; a = 4 000 FCFA, b = 300 FCFA per unit.**

lessons.title: Arithmetic and geometric sequences
lessons.programRef: Cameroon secondary (general education) Mathematics programme, Form 4 (MINESEC) — to be checked against the official programme
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence
Find the sum of an arithmetic series
Find the nth term and sum of a geometric sequence
Solve practical problems on savings and depreciation
reviewNotes: The sum to infinity of a GP and sigma notation are not included; check whether the Form 4 scheme requires them.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Arithmetic sequences
blocks.md: In an **arithmetic** sequence (AP) the **common difference** d is added each time. With first term a:

blocks.title: AP example
blocks.md: 5, 8, 11, 14, … has a = 5 and d = 3, so T_n = 5 + 3(n − 1) = 3n + 2. The 10th term is 32, and the sum of the first 10 terms is 10 ÷ 2 × (10 + 27) = 185. You can also use S = n ÷ 2 × (first term + last term) = 5 × (5 + 32) = 185.

blocks.caption: The terms 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20 of the sequence 3n + 2 plotted against n.
blocks.alt: Six points rising by 3 each time, joined by dashed lines.

blocks.title: Geometric sequences
blocks.md: In a **geometric** sequence (GP) each term is multiplied by the **common ratio** r:

blocks.title: GP example
blocks.md: 3, 6, 12, 24, … has a = 3 and r = 2. The 8th term is 3 × 2⁷ = 384. The sum of the first 6 terms is 3 × (2⁶ − 1) ÷ (2 − 1) = 189. A ratio **less than 1** means the terms decrease, e.g. depreciation of a machine by 20% a year has r = 0.8.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Using n instead of (n − 1) in the formula for the nth term.
- Confusing a sequence (a list) with a series (a sum).
- Treating a sequence as arithmetic when the ratio, not the difference, is constant.

blocks.title: Example 1: arithmetic
blocks.statement: A trader saves 5 000 FCFA in the first month and 1 500 FCFA more each month than the month before. How much does she save in month 12 and in total over 12 months?

blocks.title: Example 2: geometric
blocks.statement: Find the 8th term and the sum of the first 6 terms of 3, 6, 12, …. A machine worth 600 000 FCFA loses 20% of its value each year: find its value after 3 years.
steps: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.8: 600 000 × 0.8³ = 600 000 × 0.512.
